<STRUCT_0001>
Here is a way to reinterpret the seminormalization of a scheme
which locally has finitely many irreducible components.

Let <MATH_0001> be a scheme such that every quasi-compact open has
finitely many irreducible components. Let <MATH_0002>
be the normalization of <MATH_0003>. Then the seminormalization of <MATH_0004> in
<MATH_0005> is is the seminormalization of <MATH_0006>. In a formula:
<MATH_0007>.

Let <MATH_0001> be as in (<REF_0001>)
so that <MATH_0002> is the normalization of <MATH_0003> in <MATH_0004>.
The seminormalization <MATH_0005> of <MATH_0006> is the initial object in the
category of universal homeomorphisms <MATH_0007> inducing isomorphisms on
residue fields. Since <MATH_0008> is the disjoint union of the spectra of the
residue fields at the generic points of irreducible components of <MATH_0009>,
we see that for any <MATH_0010> in this category we obtain a canonical
lift <MATH_0011> of <MATH_0012>. Then by
Lemma <REF_0002>
we obtain a canonical morphism <MATH_0013>.
Whence in turn a canonical morphism <MATH_0014>
by the universal property of <MATH_0015>.
In this way we see that <MATH_0016> satisfies the
same universal property that <MATH_0017> has and we conclude.
